Enum.name: form_error_no

Enum.description: A form error occurred since last read of this register.
Enum.name: form_error_yes

BitField.description: Cyclic Redundancy Check Error in the CRC field of CAN FD frames with the BRS bit set
BitField.name: CRCERR_FAST

Enum.description: No such occurrence.
Enum.name: CRC_error_no

Enum.description: A CRC error occurred since last read of this register.
Enum.name: CRC_error_yes

BitField.description: Bit0 Error in the Data Phase of CAN FD frames with the BRS bit set
BitField.name: BIT0ERR_FAST

Enum.description: No such occurrence.
Enum.name: bit0_error_no

Enum.description: At least one bit sent as dominant is received as recessive.
Enum.name: bit0_error_yes

BitField.description: Bit1 Error in the Data Phase of CAN FD frames with the BRS bit set
BitField.name: BIT1ERR_FAST

Enum.description: No such occurrence.
Enum.name: bit1_error_no

Enum.description: At least one bit sent as recessive is received as dominant.
Enum.name: bit1_error_yes

BitField.description: Buffer MB0 Interrupt Or Clear FIFO bit
BitField.name: BUF0I

Enum.description: The corresponding buffer has no occurrence of successfully completed transmission or reception when MCR[RFEN]=0.
Enum.name: buffer_Tx_Rx_not_complete

Enum.description: The corresponding buffer has successfully completed transmission or reception when MCR[RFEN]=0.
Enum.name: buffer_Tx_Rx_complete

BitField.description: Buffer MB5 Interrupt Or Frames available in Rx FIFO
BitField.name: BUF5I

Enum.description: No occurrence of MB5 completing transmission/reception when MCR[RFEN]=0, or of frame(s) available in the FIFO, when MCR[RFEN]=1
Enum.name: id2

Enum.description: MB5 completed transmission/reception when MCR[RFEN]=0, or frame(s) available in the Rx FIFO when MCR[RFEN]=1. It generates a DMA request in case of MCR[RFEN] and MCR[DMA] are enabled.
Enum.name: id4

BitField.description: Buffer MB6 Interrupt Or Rx FIFO Warning
BitField.name: BUF6I

Enum.description: No occurrence of MB6 completing transmission/reception when MCR[RFEN]=0, or of Rx FIFO almost full when MCR[RFEN]=1
Enum.name: id2

Enum.description: MB6 completed transmission/reception when MCR[RFEN]=0, or Rx FIFO almost full when MCR[RFEN]=1
Enum.name: id4

BitField.description: Buffer MB7 Interrupt Or Rx FIFO Overflow
BitField.name: BUF7I

Enum.description: No occurrence of MB7 completing transmission/reception when MCR[RFEN]=0, or of Rx FIFO overflow when MCR[RFEN]=1
Enum.name: id2

Enum.description: MB7 completed transmission/reception when MCR[RFEN]=0, or Rx FIFO overflow when MCR[RFEN]=1
Enum.name: id4

Enum.description: Edge filter is enabled
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Edge filter is disabled
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: FlexCAN operates using the non-ISO CAN FD protocol.
Enum.name: non_ISO

Enum.description: FlexCAN operates using the ISO CAN FD protocol (ISO 11898-1).
Enum.name: ISO

Enum.description: Protocol exception is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Protocol exception is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: The free running timer is clocked by the CAN bit clock, which defines the baud rate on the CAN bus.
Enum.name: CAN_bit_clock

Enum.description: The free running timer is clocked by an external time tick. The period can be either adjusted to be equal to the baud rate on the CAN bus, or a different value as required. See the device-specific section for details about the external time tick.
Enum.name: external_clock

BitField.description: Entire Frame Arbitration Field Comparison Enable For Rx Mailboxes
BitField.name: EACEN

Enum.description: Rx mailbox filter's IDE bit is always compared and RTR is never compared despite mask bits.
Enum.name: RTR_compare_no

Enum.description: Enables the comparison of both Rx mailbox filter's IDE and RTR bit with their corresponding bits within the incoming frame. Mask bits do apply.
Enum.name: RTR_compare_yes

Enum.description: Remote response frame is generated.
Enum.name: remote_response_frame_not_generated

Enum.description: Remote request frame is stored.
Enum.name: remote_response_frame_generated

Enum.description: Matching starts from Rx FIFO and continues on mailboxes.
Enum.name: id2

Enum.description: Matching starts from mailboxes and continues on Rx FIFO.
Enum.name: id4

BitField.description: Write-Access To Memory In Freeze Mode
BitField.name: WRMFRZ

Enum.description: Maintain the write access restrictions.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Enable unrestricted write access to FlexCAN memory.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Disable update.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Enable update.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Bus off done interrupt disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Bus off done interrupt enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Error Interrupt Mask for errors detected in the data phase of fast CAN FD frames
BitField.name: ERRMSK_FAST

Enum.description: ERRINT_FAST error interrupt disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: ERRINT_FAST error interrupt enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: If ESR2[VPS] is asserted, the ESR2[LPTM] is not an inactive mailbox.
Enum.name: inactive_mailbox_no

Enum.description: If ESR2[VPS] is asserted, there is at least one inactive mailbox. LPTM content is the number of the first one.
Enum.name: inactive_mailbox_yes

Enum.description: Contents of IMB and LPTM are invalid.
Enum.name: invalid

Enum.description: Contents of IMB and LPTM are valid.
Enum.name: valid

Enum.description: Extended bit time definitions disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Extended bit time definitions enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.
BitField.name: DLC

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.
BitField.name: IDE

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.
BitField.name: SRR

BitField.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.
BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.
BitField.name: PRIO

BitField.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: EXT

BitField.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.
BitField.name: STD

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.
BitField.name: RTR

BitField.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.name: CODE

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.
BitField.name: ESI

BitField.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.
BitField.name: BRS

BitField.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.
BitField.name: EDL

BitField.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

BitField.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

BitField.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

BitField.description: This bit determines whether AHB RX Buffer and AHB TX Buffer will be cleaned automatically when FlexSPI returns STOP mode ACK. Software should set this bit if AHB RX Buffer or AHB TX Buffer will be powered off in STOP mode. BitField.description: Write mask option bit 1. This option bit could be used to remove AHB write burst start address alignment limitation.
BitField.name: WMOPT1

Enum.description: DQS pin will be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is no limitation on AHB write burst start address alignment when flash is accessed in individual mode.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: DQS pin will not be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is limitation on AHB write burst start address alignment when flash is accessed in individual mode.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Write mask option bit 2. When using AP memory, This option bit could be used to remove AHB write burst minimal length limitation. When using this bit, WMOPT1 should also be set.
BitField.name: WMOPT2

Enum.description: DQS pin will be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is no limitation on AHB write burst length when flash is accessed in individual mode.
Enum.name: WMOPT2_0

Enum.description: DQS pin will not be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is limitation on AHB write burst length when flash is accessed in individual mode, the minimal write burst length should be 4.
Enum.name: WMOPT2_1

BitField.description: Write mask enable bit for flash device on port A. When write mask function is needed for memory device on port A, this bit must be set.
BitField.name: WMENA

Enum.description: Write mask is disabled, DQS(RWDS) pin will be un-driven when writing to external device.
Enum.name: WMENA_0

Enum.description: Write mask is enabled, DQS(RWDS) pin will be driven by FlexSPI as write mask output when writing to external device.
Enum.name: WMENA_1

BitField.description: Write mask enable bit for flash device on port B. When write mask function is needed for memory device on port B, this bit must be set.
BitField.name: WMENB

Enum.description: Write mask is disabled, DQS(RWDS) pin will be un-driven when writing to external device.
Enum.name: WMENB_0

Enum.description: Write mask is enabled, DQS(RWDS) pin will be driven by FlexSPI as write mask output when writing to external device.
Enum.name: WMENB_1

BitField.description: Software could force a reset on DLL by setting this field to 0x1. This will cause the DLL to lose lock and re-calibrate to detect an ref_clock half period phase shift. The reset action is edge triggered, so software need to clear this bit after set this bit (no delay limitation).
BitField.name: DLLRESET

BitField.description: The delay target for slave delay line is: ((SLVDLYTARGET+1) * 1/32 * clock cycle of reference clock (serial root clock). If serial root clock is >= 100 MHz, DLLEN set to 0x1, OVRDEN set to =0x0, then SLVDLYTARGET setting of 0xF is recommended.
BitField.name: SLVDLYTARGET

BitField.description: Slave clock delay line delay cell number selection override enable.
BitField.name: OVRDEN

BitField.description: Slave clock delay line delay cell number selection override value.
BitField.name: OVRDVAL

BitField.description: Software could force a reset on DLL by setting this field to 0x1. This will cause the DLL to lose lock and re-calibrate to detect an ref_clock half period phase shift. The reset action is edge triggered, so software need to clear this bit after set this bit (no delay limitation).
BitField.name: DLLRESET

BitField.description: The delay target for slave delay line is: ((SLVDLYTARGET+1) * 1/32 * clock cycle of reference clock (serial root clock). If serial root clock is >= 100 MHz, DLLEN set to 0x1, OVRDEN set to =0x0, then SLVDLYTARGET setting of 0xF is recommended.
BitField.name: SLVDLYTARGET

BitField.description: Slave clock delay line delay cell number selection override enable.

BitField.description: AHB bus address that trigger the current ECC multi bits error interrupt.
BitField.name: AHBADDRESS

BitField.description: ECC single bit error correction indication.
BitField.name: ECCSINGLEERRORCORR

BitField.description: This status bit indicates the state machine in SEQ_CTL is idle and there is command sequence executing on FlexSPI interface.
BitField.name: SEQIDLE

BitField.description: This status bit indicates the state machine in ARB_CTL is busy and there is command sequence granted by arbitrator and not finished yet on FlexSPI interface. When ARB_CTL state (ARBIDLE=0x1) is idle, there will be no transaction on FlexSPI interface also (SEQIDLE=0x1). So this bit should be polled to wait for FlexSPI controller become idle instead of SEQIDLE.
BitField.name: ARBIDLE

BitField.description: This status field indicates the trigger source of current command sequence granted by arbitrator. This field value is meaningless when ARB_CTL is not busy (STS0[ARBIDLE]=0x1).
BitField.name: ARBCMDSRC

Enum.description: Triggered by IP command (triggered by setting register bit IPCMD.TRG).
Enum.name: ARBCMDSRC_2

Enum.description: Triggered by suspended command (resumed).
Enum.name: ARBCMDSRC_3

BitField.description: Enable AHB bus Read Access to IP RX FIFO.

BitField.description: Half Speed Serial Flash access Enable.
BitField.name: HSEN

Enum.description: Disable divide by 2 of serial flash clock for half speed commands.
Enum.name: HSEN_0

Enum.description: Enable divide by 2 of serial flash clock for half speed commands.
Enum.name: HSEN_1

Enum.description: Doze mode support disabled. AHB clock and serial clock will not be gated off when there is doze mode request from system.
Enum.name: DOZEEN_0

Enum.description: Doze mode support enabled. AHB clock and serial clock will be gated off when there is doze mode request from system.
Enum.name: DOZEEN_1

BitField.description: This bit is to support Flash Octal mode access by combining Port A and B Data pins (A_DATA[3:0] and B_DATA[3:0]), when Port A and Port B are of 4 bit data width.
BitField.name: COMBINATIONEN

BitField.description: This bit is used to force SCLK output free-running. For FPGA applications, external device may use SCLK as reference clock to its internal PLL. If SCLK free-running is enabled, data sampling with loopback clock from SCLK pad is not supported (MCR0[RXCLKSRC]=2).
BitField.name: SCKFREERUNEN

BitField.description: Time out wait cycle for IP command grant.
BitField.name: IPGRANTWAIT

BitField.description: Timeout wait cycle for AHB command grant.
BitField.name: AHBGRANTWAIT

BitField.description: AHB Read/Write access to Serial Flash Memory space will timeout if not data received from Flash or data not transmitted after AHBBUSWAIT * 1024 ahb clock cycles, AHB Bus will get an error response
BitField.name: AHBBUSWAIT

BitField.description: Command Sequence Execution will timeout and abort after SEQWAIT * 1024 Serial Root Clock cycles
BitField.name: SEQWAIT

BitField.description: This bit determines whether AHB RX Buffer and AHB TX Buffer will be cleaned automatically when FlexSPI returns STOP mode ACK. Software should set this bit if AHB RX Buffer or AHB TX Buffer will be powered off in STOP mode. Otherwise AHB read access after exiting STOP mode may hit AHB RX Buffer or AHB TX Buffer but their data entries are invalid.
BitField.name: CLRAHBBUFOPT

Enum.description: AHB RX/TX Buffer will not be cleaned automatically when FlexSPI return Stop mode ACK.
Enum.name: CLRAHBBUFOPT_0

Enum.description: AHB RX/TX Buffer will be cleaned automatically when FlexSPI return Stop mode ACK.
Enum.name: CLRAHBBUFOPT_1

BitField.description: All external devices are same devices (both in types and size) for A1/A2/B1/B2.
BitField.name: SAMEDEVICEEN

Enum.description: In Individual mode, FLSHA1CRx/FLSHA2CRx/FLSHB1CRx/FLSHB2CRx register setting will be applied to Flash A1/A2/B1/B2 separately. In Parallel mode, FLSHA1CRx register setting will be applied to Flash A1 and B1, FLSHA2CRx register setting will be applied to Flash A2 and B2. FLSHB1CRx/FLSHB2CRx register settings will be ignored.
Enum.name: individual_parallel

Enum.description: FLSHA1CR0/FLSHA1CR1/FLSHA1CR2 register settings will be applied to Flash A1/A2/B1/B2. FLSHA2CRx/FLSHB1CRx/FLSHB2CRx will be ignored.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: B_SCLK pad can be used as A_SCLK differential clock output (inverted clock to A_SCLK). In this case, port B flash access is not available. After changing the value of this field, MCR0[SWRESET] should be set.
BitField.name: SCKBDIFFOPT

Enum.description: B_SCLK pad is used as port B SCLK clock output. Port B flash access is available.
Enum.name: SCKBDIFFOPT_0

Enum.description: B_SCLK pad is used as port A SCLK inverted clock output (Differential clock to A_SCLK). Port B flash access is not available.
Enum.name: SCKBDIFFOPT_1

BitField.description: Wait cycle (in AHB clock cycle) for idle state before suspended command sequence resumed.
BitField.name: RESUMEWAIT

BitField.description: Parallel mode enabled for AHB triggered Command (both read and write) .
BitField.name: APAREN

Enum.description: Flash will be accessed in Individual mode.
Enum.name: individual

Enum.description: Flash will be accessed in Parallel mode.

BitField.description: Clear the status/pointers of AHB RX Buffer. Auto-cleared.
BitField.name: CLRAHBRXBUF

BitField.description: Enable AHB bus cachable read access support.
BitField.name: CACHABLEEN

Enum.description: Disabled. When there is AHB bus cachable read access, FlexSPI will not check whether it hit AHB TX Buffer.
Enum.name: CACHABLEEN_0

Enum.description: Enabled. When there is AHB bus cachable read access, FlexSPI will check whether it hit AHB TX Buffer first.
Enum.name: CACHABLEEN_1

BitField.description: Enable AHB bus bufferable write access support. This field affects the last beat of AHB write access, refer for more details about AHB bufferable write.
BitField.name: BUFFERABLEEN

Enum.description: Disabled. For all AHB write access (no matter bufferable or non-bufferable ), FlexSPI will return AHB Bus ready after all data is transmitted to External device and AHB command finished.
Enum.name: BUFFERABLEEN_0

Enum.description: Enabled. For AHB bufferable write access, FlexSPI will return AHB Bus ready when the AHB command is granted by arbitrator and will not wait for AHB command finished.
Enum.name: BUFFERABLEEN_1

BitField.description: AHB Read Address option bit. This option bit is intend to remove AHB burst start address alignment limitation.

Enum.description: There is no AHB read burst start address alignment limitation. FlexSPI will fetch more data than AHB burst required to meet the alignment requirement.

Enum.description: AHB read size will be decided by other register setting like PREFETCH_EN,OTFAD_EN...

BitField.description: Write mask option bit 1. This option bit could be used to remove AHB write burst start address alignment limitation.
BitField.name: WMOPT1

Enum.description: DQS pin will be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is no limitation on AHB write burst start address alignment when flash is accessed in individual mode.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: DQS pin will not be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is limitation on AHB write burst start address alignment when flash is accessed in individual mode.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Write mask option bit 2. When using AP memory, This option bit could be used to remove AHB write burst minimal length limitation. When using this bit, WMOPT1 should also be set.
BitField.name: WMOPT2

Enum.description: DQS pin will be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is no limitation on AHB write burst length when flash is accessed in individual mode.
Enum.name: WMOPT2_0

Enum.description: DQS pin will not be used as Write Mask when writing to external device. There is limitation on AHB write burst length when flash is accessed in individual mode, the minimal write burst length should be 4.
Enum.name: WMOPT2_1

BitField.description: Write mask enable bit for flash device on port A. When write mask function is needed for memory device on port A, this bit must be set.
BitField.name: WMENA

Enum.description: Write mask is disabled, DQS(RWDS) pin will be un-driven when writing to external device.
Enum.name: WMENA_0

BitField.description: Software could force a reset on DLL by setting this field to 0x1. This will cause the DLL to lose lock and re-calibrate to detect an ref_clock half period phase shift. The reset action is edge triggered, so software need to clear this bit after set this bit (no delay limitation).

BitField.description: The delay target for slave delay line is: ((SLVDLYTARGET+1) * 1/32 * clock cycle of reference clock (serial root clock). If serial root clock is >= 100 MHz, DLLEN set to 0x1, OVRDEN set to =0x0, then SLVDLYTARGET setting of 0xF is recommended.
BitField.name: SLVDLYTARGET

BitField.description: This status bit indicates the state machine in SEQ_CTL is idle and there is command sequence executing on FlexSPI interface.
BitField.name: SEQIDLE

BitField.description: This status bit indicates the state machine in ARB_CTL is busy and there is command sequence granted by arbitrator and not finished yet on FlexSPI interface. When ARB_CTL state (ARBIDLE=0x1) is idle, there will be no transaction on FlexSPI interface also (SEQIDLE=0x1). So this bit should be polled to wait for FlexSPI controller become idle instead of SEQIDLE.
BitField.name: ARBIDLE

Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and continue from $0000.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_SECONDARY

Enum.name: CLEAR_ON_ROLLOVER

Enum.name: ENABLE_GATED_OUT

Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Count up.
Enum.name: COUNTUP

Enum.description: Count down.
Enum.name: COUNTDOWN

Enum.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and continue from $0000.
Enum.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: Count repeatedly.
Enum.name: REPEAT

Enum.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.
Enum.name: UNTIL_COMPARE

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: A logic 0 on the fault input indicates a fault condition.
Enum.name: LOGIC_0

Enum.description: A logic 1 on the fault input indicates a fault condition.
Enum.name: LOGIC_1

Enum.description: No fault on the FAULTx pin.
Enum.name: NO_FLAG

Enum.description: Fault on the FAULTx pin.
Enum.name: FLAG

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO

Enum.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.
Enum.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN

Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: SAFE

Enum.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].
Enum.name: MANUAL

Enum.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Indicates to the transmit data FIFO that the written frames contain two additional octets before the frame data. This means the actual frame begins at bit 16 of the first word written into the FIFO. This function allows putting the frame payload on a 32-bit boundary in memory, as the 14-byte Ethernet header is extended to a 16-byte header.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enables insertion of IP header checksum.
BitField.name: IPCHK

Enum.description: Checksum is not inserted.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IP frame is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically. The IP header checksum field must be cleared. If a non-IP frame is transmitted the frame is not modified.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: Checksum not inserted.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IP frame with a known protocol is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically into the frame. The checksum field must be cleared. The other frames are not modified.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Padding Removal For Short IP Frames
BitField.name: PADREM

Enum.description: Padding not removed.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Any bytes following the IP payload section of the frame are removed from the frame.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong IPv4 Header Checksum
BitField.name: IPDIS

Enum.description: Frames with wrong IPv4 header checksum are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IPv4 frame is received with a mismatching header checksum, the frame is discarded. IPv6 has no header checksum and is not affected by this setting. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong Protocol Checksum
BitField.name: PRODIS

Enum.description: Frames with wrong checksum are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If a TCP/IP, UDP/IP, or ICMP/IP frame is received that has a wrong TCP, UDP, or ICMP checksum, the frame is discarded. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With MAC Layer Errors
BitField.name: LINEDIS

Enum.description: Frames with errors are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Any frame received with a CRC, length, or PHY error is automatically discarded and not forwarded to the user application interface.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: Instructs the MAC to write two additional bytes in front of each frame received into the RX FIFO.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: The traffic shaper function should consider 12 octets of IPG in addition to the frame data transferred for a frame when doing bandwidth calculations. This is the default.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Addition of 12 bytes for the IPG should be omitted when calculating the bandwidth (for traffic shaping, when writing a frame into the transmit FIFO, the shaper will usually consider 12 bytes of IPG for every frame as part of the bandwidth allocated by the frame. This addition can be suppressed, meaning short frames will become more bandwidth than large frames due to the relation of data to IPG overhead).

Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: A period event interrupt can be generated (EIR[TS_TIMER]) and the event signal output is asserted when the timer wraps around according to the periodic setting ATPER. Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: Indicates to the transmit data FIFO that the written frames contain two additional octets before the frame data. This means the actual frame begins at bit 16 of the first word written into the FIFO. This function allows putting the frame payload on a 32-bit boundary in memory, as the 14-byte Ethernet header is extended to a 16-byte header.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enables insertion of IP header checksum.
BitField.name: IPCHK

Enum.description: Checksum is not inserted.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IP frame is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically. The IP header checksum field must be cleared. If a non-IP frame is transmitted the frame is not modified.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: Checksum not inserted.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IP frame with a known protocol is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically into the frame. The checksum field must be cleared. The other frames are not modified.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Padding Removal For Short IP Frames
BitField.name: PADREM

Enum.description: Padding not removed.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Any bytes following the IP payload section of the frame are removed from the frame.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong IPv4 Header Checksum
BitField.name: IPDIS

Enum.description: Frames with wrong IPv4 header checksum are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If an IPv4 frame is received with a mismatching header checksum, the frame is discarded. IPv6 has no header checksum and is not affected by this setting. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong Protocol Checksum
BitField.name: PRODIS

Enum.description: Frames with wrong checksum are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If a TCP/IP, UDP/IP, or ICMP/IP frame is received that has a wrong TCP, UDP, or ICMP checksum, the frame is discarded. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With MAC Layer Errors
BitField.name: LINEDIS

Enum.description: Frames with errors are not discarded.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: Any frame received with a CRC, length, or PHY error is automatically discarded and not forwarded to the user application interface.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: Instructs the MAC to write two additional bytes in front of each frame received into the RX FIFO.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: The timer stops at the current value.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: The timer starts incrementing.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: The timer can be reset to zero when the given offset time is reached (offset event). The field is cleared when the offset event is reached, so no further event occurs until the field is set again. The timer offset value must be set before setting this field.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: The timer is not affected and no action occurs, besides clearing OFFEN, when the offset is reached.
Enum.name: ZERO

Enum.description: If OFFEN is set, the timer resets to zero when the offset setting is reached. The offset event does not cause a timer interrupt.
Enum.name: ONE

Enum.description: A period event interrupt can be generated (EIR[TS_TIMER]) and the event signal output is asserted when the timer wraps around according to the periodic setting ATPER. The timer period value must be set before setting this bit. Not all devices contain the event signal output. See the chip configuration details.
Enum.name: ONE

BitField.name: PINPER

Enum.description: Stop Mode. Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G1_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G1_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G1_SMBLOB, G1_WRITE and G1_READ settings.
Enum.name: G1_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G1_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G1_READ and G1_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G1_SM_B_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G2_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G2_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G2_SMBLOB, G2_WRITE and G2_READ settings.
Enum.name: G2_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G2_READ and G2_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of these registers.
Enum.name: SMAG_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are locked. The SMAG2JR and SMAG1JR registers cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs.
Enum.name: SMAG_LOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of the SMAP register.
Enum.name: SMAP_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is locked. The SMAP_LCK, CSP and PSP bits and G1 and G2 permission bits of the SMAP register cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs. The PARTITION_KMOD value can still be changed. The SMAG_LCK bit can be changed to a 1, but cannot be changed to a 0.
Enum.name: SMAP_LOCKED

Enum.description: The partition and any of the pages allocated to the partition can be de-allocated.
Enum.name: NOT_DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The partition cannot be de-allocated and the pages allocated to the partition cannot be de-allocated.
Enum.name: DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will not be zeroized when they are de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: NOT_ZEROIZED

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will be zeroized when they are individually de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: ZEROIZED

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G1_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G1_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G1_SMBLOB, G1_WRITE and G1_READ settings.
Enum.name: G1_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G1_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G1_READ and G1_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G1_SM_B_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G2_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G2_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G2_SMBLOB, G2_WRITE and G2_READ settings.
Enum.name: G2_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G2_READ and G2_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of these registers.
Enum.name: SMAG_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are locked. The SMAG2JR and SMAG1JR registers cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs.
Enum.name: SMAG_LOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of the SMAP register.
Enum.name: SMAP_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is locked. The SMAP_LCK, CSP and PSP bits and G1 and G2 permission bits of the SMAP register cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs. The PARTITION_KMOD value can still be changed. The SMAG_LCK bit can be changed to a 1, but cannot be changed to a 0.
Enum.name: SMAP_LOCKED

Enum.description: The partition and any of the pages allocated to the partition can be de-allocated.
Enum.name: NOT_DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The partition cannot be de-allocated and the pages allocated to the partition cannot be de-allocated.
Enum.name: DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will not be zeroized when they are de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: NOT_ZEROIZED

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will be zeroized when they are individually de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: ZEROIZED

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G1_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G1_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G1_SMBLOB, G1_WRITE and G1_READ settings.
Enum.name: G1_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G1_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G1_READ and G1_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G1_SM_B_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G2_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G2_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G2_SMBLOB, G2_WRITE and G2_READ settings.
Enum.name: G2_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G2_READ and G2_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of these registers.
Enum.name: SMAG_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are locked. The SMAG2JR and SMAG1JR registers cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs.
Enum.name: SMAG_LOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of the SMAP register.
Enum.name: SMAP_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is locked. The SMAP_LCK, CSP and PSP bits and G1 and G2 permission bits of the SMAP register cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs. The PARTITION_KMOD value can still be changed. The SMAG_LCK bit can be changed to a 1, but cannot be changed to a 0.
Enum.name: SMAP_LOCKED

Enum.description: The partition and any of the pages allocated to the partition can be de-allocated.
Enum.name: NOT_DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The partition cannot be de-allocated and the pages allocated to the partition cannot be de-allocated.
Enum.name: DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will not be zeroized when they are de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: NOT_ZEROIZED

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will be zeroized when they are individually de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: ZEROIZED

BitField.description: The value in this field is used to modify the Blob Key Encryption Key when exporting cryptographic Blobs from, or importing cryptographic Blobs to, this partition
BitField.name: PARTITION_KMOD

BitField.description: Command: 1h: Allocate Page - This command allocates the page specified in the PAGE field to the partition specified in the PRTN field
BitField.name: CMD

BitField.description: Partition: When an Allocate Page or De-allocate Partition command is issued, the action is performed on the partition indicated in the PRTN field
BitField.name: PRTN

BitField.description: This is the number of the page to be referenced in field CMD
BitField.name: PAGE

BitField.description: Following a Page Inquiry Command, if the PO field is 10 or 11, this field indicates the partition to which the page specified in the PAGE field is allocated
BitField.name: PRTN

BitField.description: Page Owner: Following a Page Inquiry Command, this field indicates if the Page is owned by the entity that issued the inquiry, owned by another entity, or unowned
BitField.name: PO

Enum.description: Available; Unowned: The entity that issued the inquiry may allocate this page to a partition. No zeroization is needed since it has already been cleared, therefore no interrupt should be expected.
Enum.name: AVAILABLE

Enum.description: Page does not exist in this version or is not initialized yet.
Enum.name: NOT_PRESENT_OR_INITIALIZED

Enum.description: Another entity owns the page. This page is unavailable to the issuer of the inquiry.
Enum.name: UNAVAILABLE

Enum.description: Owned by the entity making the inquiry. The owner may de-allocate this page if its partition is not marked PSP. If the partition to which the page is allocated is designated as CSP, the page will be zeroized upon de-allocation.
Enum.name: OWNED

Enum.description: No Error.
Enum.name: NO_ERROR

Enum.description: Command has not yet completed.
Enum.name: CMD_INCOMPLETE_ERROR

Enum.description: A security failure occurred.
Enum.name: SECURITY_FAILURE

Enum.description: Command Overflow. Another command was issued by the same Job Ring owner before the owner's previous command completed. The additional command was ignored.
Enum.name: CMD_OVERFLOW_ERROR

Enum.description: Interrupt enabled.
Enum.name: INTR_ENABLED

Enum.description: Interrupt masked.
Enum.name: INTR_MASKED

Enum.description: Interrupt coalescing is disabled. If the IMSK bit is cleared, an interrupt is asserted whenever a job is written to the output ring. ICDCT is ignored. Note that if software removes one or more jobs and clears the interrupt but the output rings slots full is still greater than 0 (ORSF > 0), then the interrupt will clear but reassert on the next clock cycle.
Enum.name: INTR_COAL_DISABLED

Enum.description: Interrupt coalescing is enabled. If the IMSK bit is cleared, an interrupt is asserted whenever the threshold number of frames is reached (ICDCT) or when the threshold timer expires (ICTT). Note that if software removes one or more jobs and clears the interrupt but the interrupt coalescing threshold is still met (ORSF >= ICDCT), then the interrupt will clear but reassert on the next clock cycle.
Enum.name: INTR_COAL_ENABLED

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G1_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G1_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G1_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G1_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G1_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G1_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G1_SMBLOB, G1_WRITE and G1_READ settings.
Enum.name: G1_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G1_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G1_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G1_READ and G1_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G1_SM_B_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor reads (if G2_TDO=1) and key-reads are always allowed, and exporting Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_READ_PROHIB

Enum.description: Instruction fetches and reads are allowed (but exporting a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_READ_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Writes are prohibited (except that Trusted Descriptor writes are allowed, and importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed if G2_SMBLOB=1 or if done by a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_PROHIB

Enum.description: Writes are allowed (but importing a Secure Memory Blob is prohibited if G2_SMBLOB=0 and the descriptor is not a Trusted Descriptor or if G2_TDO=0).
Enum.name: G2_WRITE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors have the same access privileges as Job Descriptors
Enum.name: G2_TD_PRIVILEGE_AS_JD

Enum.description: Trusted Descriptors are allowed to override the other access permissions, i.e. they can export blobs from or import blobs to the partition and read from and write to the partition regardless of the G2_SMBLOB, G2_WRITE and G2_READ settings.
Enum.name: G2_TD_OVERIDE_ALLOWED

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is prohibited, unless done via a Trusted Descriptor and G2_TDO=1.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_PROHIB

Enum.description: Exporting or importing Secure Memory Blobs is allowed, regardless of the G2_READ and G2_WRITE settings.
Enum.name: G2_SM_BLOB_EXPORT_IMPORT_ALLOWED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of these registers.
Enum.name: SMAG_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAG2JR register and SMAG1JR register are locked. The SMAG2JR and SMAG1JR registers cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs.
Enum.name: SMAG_LOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is unlocked. The partition owner can change any writable bits of the SMAP register.
Enum.name: SMAP_UNLOCKED

Enum.description: The SMAP register is locked. The SMAP_LCK, CSP and PSP bits and G1 and G2 permission bits of the SMAP register cannot be changed until the partition is de-allocated or a POR occurs. The PARTITION_KMOD value can still be changed. The SMAG_LCK bit can be changed to a 1, but cannot be changed to a 0.
Enum.name: SMAP_LOCKED

Enum.description: The partition and any of the pages allocated to the partition can be de-allocated.
Enum.name: NOT_DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The partition cannot be de-allocated and the pages allocated to the partition cannot be de-allocated.
Enum.name: DEALLOCATABLE

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will not be zeroized when they are de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: NOT_ZEROIZED

Enum.description: The pages allocated to the partition will be zeroized when they are individually de-allocated or the partition is released or a security alarm occurs.
Enum.name: ZEROIZED

BitField.description: Command: 1h: Allocate Page - This command allocates the page specified in the PAGE field to the partition specified in the PRTN field
BitField.name: CMD

BitField.description: Partition: When an Allocate Page or De-allocate Partition command is issued, the action is performed on the partition indicated in the PRTN field
BitField.name: PRTN

BitField.description: This is the number of the page to be referenced in field CMD
BitField.name: PAGE

BitField.description: Following a Page Inquiry Command, if the PO field is 10 or 11, this field indicates the partition to which the page specified in the PAGE field is allocated
BitField.name: PRTN

BitField.description: Page Owner: Following a Page Inquiry Command, this field indicates if the Page is owned by the entity that issued the inquiry, owned by another entity, or unowned
BitField.name: PO

Enum.description: Available; Unowned: The entity that issued the inquiry may allocate this page to a partition. No zeroization is needed since it has already been cleared, therefore no interrupt should be expected.
Enum.name: AVAILABLE

Enum.description: Page does not exist in this version or is not initialized yet.
Enum.name: NOT_PRESENT_OR_INITIALIZED

Enum.description: Another entity owns the page. This page is unavailable to the issuer of the inquiry.
Enum.name: UNAVAILABLE

Enum.description: Owned by the entity making the inquiry. The owner may de-allocate this page if its partition is not marked PSP. If the partition to which the page is allocated is designated as CSP, the page will be zeroized upon de-allocation.
Enum.name: OWNED

Enum.description: No Error.
Enum.name: NO_ERROR

Enum.description: Command has not yet completed.
Enum.name: CMD_INCOMPLETE_ERROR

Enum.description: A security failure occurred.
Enum.name: SECURITY_FAILURE

Enum.description: Command Overflow. Another command was issued by the same Job Ring owner before the owner's previous command completed. The additional command was ignored.
Enum.name: CMD_OVERFLOW_ERROR

Register.description: Recoverable Error Interrupt Record 0 for Job Ring 0
Register.name: REIR0JR0

BitField.description: This field indicates the type of the recoverable error
BitField.name: TYPE

BitField.description: If MISS=1, a second recoverable error associated with JR occurred before REIR0JR was written following a previous JR recoverable error
BitField.name: MISS

Register.description: Recoverable Error Interrupt Record 2 for Job Ring 0
Register.name: REIR2JR0

BitField.description: Address associated with the recoverable JR error.
BitField.name: ADDR

Register.description: Recoverable Error Interrupt Record 4 for Job Ring 0
Register.name: REIR4JR0

BitField.description: This field holds the ICID associated with the recoverable error.
BitField.name: ICID

BitField.description: This field holds the DID associated with the recoverable error.
BitField.name: DID

BitField.description: This field holds the AXI cache control transaction attribute used for the memory access.
BitField.name: AXCACHE

BitField.description: This field holds the AXI protection transaction attribute used for the memory access.
BitField.name: AXPROT

BitField.description: This field specifies whether the memory access was a read or write.
BitField.name: RWB

BitField.description: This field holds the AXI error response associated with the recoverable error.
BitField.name: ERR

BitField.description: This field holds the memory interface index associated with the recoverable error.
BitField.name: MIX

Register.description: Recoverable Error Interrupt Record 5 for Job Ring 0
Register.name: REIR5JR0

BitField.description: This field holds the block identifier (see Internal Block ID) of the source of the AXI transaction associated with the recoverable error
BitField.name: BID

BitField.description: This field indicates whether the bus transaction associated with the recoverable error was initiating an CAAM Secure Memory blob operation
BitField.name: BNDG

BitField.description: This field indicates whether the bus transaction associated with the recoverable error was an attempt to assert trusted descriptor privilege when accessing an CAAM Secure Memory partition
BitField.name: TDSC

BitField.description: This field indicates whether the bus transaction associated with the recoverable error was an attempt to read the key modifier associated with an CAAM Secure Memory partition
BitField.name: KMOD

BitField.description: This field indicates whether the bus transaction associated with the recoverable error was an attempted key access to CAAM Secure Memory
BitField.name: KEY

BitField.description: This field indicates whether the bus transaction associated with the recoverable error was an attempted access to CAAM Secure Memory
BitField.name: SMA
